reasons: Deviation classification is correct: § 12.1's grant is expressly 'revocable' with no trigger (revocation at IBM's discretion) and names only Customer, so it fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice) and sits in walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it adds 'its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf', deletes 'revocable' at will, and substitutes revocation only for Customer's uncured material breach after written notice — matching the preferred position for a subscription/services licence.
Scope is appropriately limited: successor transfer is not duplicated because § 14.10 already permits assignment to a successor by merger/acquisition, avoiding double-flagging.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the affiliates-on-notice fallback.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (ratio 0.614) is explained by the need to rewrite the grant sentence to both extend the licensee set and convert at-will revocability; no unnecessary substantive changes were introduced and the surrounding restrictions were left intact.
